title: Outreach: letterbox drops
question: Three ways to organise the same feature (plan an area, walk both sides of every street, count letterboxes and bundles, and share coverage so streets aren't done twice in a week). Lock the one that should lead; the others can live inside it.

options.label: Patch board
options.lineage: a parish map cut into delivery runs
options.thesis: The area around the church is pre-cut into patches of about one bundle each, coloured by when they were last done; claim one near you and walk it.
options.viewport: Navy masthead with this week's coverage; a map of patches tinted fresh, claimed or done; a sheet suggesting the freshest patch near your address with letterboxes, loop length and Claim.
options.risk: You choose patches, not kilometres: '3 km from home' becomes 'one or two patches near home', and patches must be cut and kept up to date.

options.label: Route from your door
options.thesis: Enter an address and a distance; a loop covering both sides of every street redraws live, with letterbox and bundle counts, steering around streets done this week.
options.viewport: Full-screen map with the loop and start pin; a sheet with Start (Home, Church, Other), a distance stepper, letterboxes, bundles and time, and Start walk.
options.risk: Everyone picks their own area, so coverage gets lumpy unless the generator pushes hard toward fresh streets.

options.label: Outreach day board
options.lineage: a team run sheet on a clipboard
options.thesis: An outreach day as a run sheet: each team a row with its route, bundles and live progress, plus the month's coverage of the suburb.
options.viewport: Masthead with the day's totals; Teams / Map tabs; a row per team with names, patch, bundles and progress; coverage this month at the foot.
options.risk: Needs sign-in and a leader role, and it does little for someone walking alone on a Tuesday.
